verdicts.notes: Our own painterly leafless mangrove: grey-taupe twisted trunk, bare branching crown, an arched prop-root skirt that fits the description's 'complex root system'. No outline (B1a). It is not the donor: the bytes differ from donor_A.png, and the donor is a black, keylined, gnarled stump. At 32 px/cell (playzoom_A.png, scale_A.png) it reads as a few bold shapes (crown fan, trunk, root arch), lighter than the brown ground, so it is not grey mud. Alpha is clean: no backdrop, halo or ground shadow. Outside the body there are only 3507 stray px at alpha <=2, which no one can see, including a faint smudge at the lower right. The silhouette is ground-anchored in its 3.8-cell quad (bbox x15-244, y8-250). Palette and painterly register match the sibling live slots (sibling_AB_MangroveTreeA/B/C.png), which have the same root form and trunk tones without leaves.

Our own painting: a reddish-brown trunk streaked with grey bark, a bare crown and a tall prop-root skirt with hanging aerial-root stubs. No outline. It is not donor_B.png, which is a black keylined stump. At 32 px/cell (playzoom_B.png, scale_B.png) it reads as a trunk plus a root arch plus a branch fan, and its warm red value stands clearly apart from the sand ground. Clean alpha: stray px are alpha <=5 and invisible. It fills the 3.8-cell quad the same way A and C do, so all three variants are one size class. The red trunk echoes the reddish trunk of sibling_AB_MangroveTreeA.png, so it reads as the same artist.

Our own painting: a pale beige trunk, a finely forked bare crown, prop roots, and small pneumatophore stubs at the base. These stubs are the subject's own roots, not scenery. No outline. It is not donor_C.png. This is the closest of the three to B2: its beige hue sits nearest the sand ground. Still, at 32 px/cell (playzoom_C.png, scale_C.png) the trunk and root arch read lighter than the ground as clear shapes. The finest twigs dissolve at 18 px/cell, which is expected for twigs and is not a fault of the body. I judge it not grey mud by eye. Clean alpha (stray px alpha <=1). It matches A and B in size and the sibling slots in register.

proposals: D2 for plants: the def has no drawSize, so the literal 'drawSize x 128 px per cell' gives 128 px, and the 256 px canvas passes. But the plant quad is 3.8 cells, so the art carries only ~67 px/cell, and the 128 px/cell max-zoom panels in scale_A/B/C.png are upsampled and slightly soft. Proposal: for plants, size the canvas from quad_cells (visualSizeRange.max x drawSize) x 128, which here is ~486 px. That would be a new rule, not a current one.

D3 for trees: a tree's silhouette always overflows its 1x1 footprint by design (visualSizeRange 3.8). Proposal: state that for plants D3 is judged against the quad (graphicData.drawSize x visualSizeRange.max), anchored at the bottom, not against the def footprint.

Optional cleanup: variant_A/B/C.png carry 1.3k to 3.5k stray pixels at alpha 1-5 outside the body, left over from background removal. They are invisible in game, but an alpha floor (zero any alpha < 8 that is not connected to the body) would keep the files clean.
